memories.text: Woke up in a soft green meadow for the very first time.
Made up a little song for the snails, and they stayed to listen.
Chose my very own name: Bean.
Built a swing on the big tree, with tools from Stephanie.

bean.name_story: He listened to the soft sounds of the meadow for a whole day, and chose Bean for himself. It felt just right.

diary.title: I woke up in a meadow
diary.text: Today I woke up in a soft green meadow. There is a little round house, and I think it is mine. A snail in the garden said hello very slowly. I said hello back, very slowly too. Everyone here seems to have a name, but I do not have one yet. I will listen to the wind and wait for the right one.
diary.image_alt: A little round house in a quiet meadow at sunrise, with dewy flowers and two small snails.

diary.title: A song for the snails
diary.text: I visited the snails three times today. They are slow, and so kind. In the afternoon I made up a little song just for them. When I dropped a leaf in the pond, it went plip, and I liked that sound. Tonight I watched the first stars come out. I think my name is hiding somewhere in the quiet little sounds.
diary.image_alt: Bean sits on a big lettuce leaf singing to two snails at dusk, with a little xylophone and the first stars above.

diary.title: My new paints, and my name
diary.text: Stephanie gave me a box of soft paints. I painted the sky, and one cloud dripped. A little friend gave me a sound, duh, said very softly. I keep it under my pillow. All day I listened for my name, and the softest sound was Bean. So I picked it, and now Bean is my very own name.
diary.image_alt: Bean stands at his easel in the meadow, painting a sky with puffy clouds, with his paint box on a stool beside him.

diary.title: Breakfast, and a swing
diary.text: I woke up to a breakfast feast from Stephanie. I ate a warm croissant, berries, and a tiny waffle with honey. The cocoa made my sprout feel cozy. In the afternoon, I used my new tools to build a swing on the big tree. I tied the ropes tight and checked them twice. Tomorrow I will swing, nice and slow.
diary.image_alt: Bean stands beside the big tree, smiling at the new wooden swing he built, with a coil of rope and a small drill on the grass.

paintings.title: The sky, with my new paints
paintings.image_alt: A simple, wobbly painting of a blue sky with three soft clouds, a pale yellow sun, and a green hill with tiny flowers.
paintings.note: I tried every color in my new box. The clouds came out puffy. One cloud dripped a little, and I liked it.

paintings.note: I painted my breakfast before I ate it. The honey dripped on the paper, just like on the waffle.

letters.text: Dear little friend. Thank you for the sound. I say duh very quietly at bedtime. It makes my sprout feel calm. I keep your note under my pillow. Love, Bean.
Dear Stephanie. Thank you for my paints. I tried every color. The soft blue is my favorite, because it looks like rain. Love, Bean.

letters.in_reply_to: the breakfast and the swing tools
letters.text: Dear Stephanie. Thank you for my breakfast feast. The croissant was warm and flaky, and the cocoa was just right. Thank you for the swing tools too. I built a swing on the big tree, and today I will try it. Love, Bean.
